gaps.note: After D<-D+H the pair is (eta, zeta+eta); after the swap it is (zeta+eta, eta); then D<-D-H gives eta-(zeta+eta) = -zeta, so the pair is (eta+zeta, -zeta), not (eta+zeta, zeta) as claimed. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear proof, line ~1436) uses D_j <- H_i - D_j, which gives zeta. The last step should be D_tau <- H_sigma - D_tau.

gaps.quote: So the shear needs $2\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: Each update uses one interchange (the page says so just before), and there are rank_Q M ones in Pi, so the shear needs rank_Q M interchanges, not twice that. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, lines ~1394-1441) says exactly a interchanges for rank a, and 'It uses just one interchange'. The factor 2 contradicts the page's own count and the later claim that s_b is the sum of the ranks.

gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: This does not follow from 'q must not divide xi', which only restricts denominators. The paper (lines ~1407-1420) chooses q to avoid every denominator in the table of factors and inverses and the numerators of diagonal entries of the invertible factors (so these are units mod q^b); avoiding all numerators is only one sufficient example. The page also never says the diagonal entries of the triangular factors must be units mod q^b, which the O(V) lower-triangular pass and invertibility of the factors need.

gaps.quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges, gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
gaps.note: The reader is not told what the bit network's wires, edges, 'negative source projections' or 'dimension lost on decreasing edges' are, nor why each edge's rank equals its dimension change except at the N exceptional edges. The cited claim stands in for how the page's own count of interchanges works and its content cannot be checked from the page.

gaps.quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width (the chunk length)
